narrative:
The model predicts that you have a 32% chance of failing your final year, which indicates a significant risk of not passing. This prediction is based on several factors that have been shown to influence student outcomes.

One of the most critical aspects is your desire for higher education. The model suggests that this ambition, while positive, may not be enough to counterbalance other challenges you face. Additionally, the reason you chose your school—primarily for its proximity to home—may not provide the same motivational boost as those who selected schools based on reputation or specific courses. 

Your history of past failures also plays a role; having one previous failure can weigh heavily on your current performance, especially when compared to students who have not experienced any setbacks. This can create a cycle of struggle that is hard to break. 

Moreover, your current health status is concerning, as it is rated as very bad. This can significantly impact your ability to focus and perform academically. Lastly, your relatively high number of absences—eight compared to the average of about four—suggests that you may be missing out on crucial learning opportunities.

To improve your academic performance, consider seeking additional support, such as tutoring or study groups, and addressing your health issues. Increasing your study time and finding ways to engage more deeply with your coursework could also help you turn this situation around.
